Quick triage notes:
- Correlation: p99 spikes strongly correlated with requests where the context length > 16k tokens (not a simple linear increase; appears to be tail amplification at ~20k+).
- Error signature: increased 502/504 and transient internal 429 in one routing layer (queue saturation).
- Region: majority of traffic from us-west-2.
- Early hypothesis: cache miss rate for large KV caches + batching behavior causes long serialization in the serving runtime; also a spike in multi-tenant batch mixing for long windows.

I'll open JIRA RD-2147 and attach request traces. Stephanie — can SRE push a temporary routing rule to cap concurrent long-window requests for MindBridge? We should also consider an automatic model-variant fallback for requests whose token count > 16k to a quantized/fast variant while preserving output quality.

Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.com

Attachments: runbook_routing_patch.md

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-21T01:10:00Z
Subject: RE: JIRA RD-2147: routing/serving mitigations for long-context tail

Triage update and proposed mitigations (SRE):
1) Short-term (next 0–3 hours):
   - Enable tenant-level concurrent long-window cap: throttle requests with token_count > 16000 to 5 concurrent calls per tenant.
   - Enable model-fallback rule for >16000 tokens to the 16k-compat variant with KV-sharded cache on a canary subset (10% of traffic).
   - Push a routing policy change to prefer region eu-west-1 / us-west-2 fallbacks that have lower batch-mixing for these flows.
2) Medium-term (24–72 hours):
   - Deploy a serving runtime patch to reduce KV cache miss penalty for sharded large-context workloads (patch attached: runbook_routing_patch.md).
   - Add instrumentation to expose long-window batch composition metrics to Grafana.
3) Customer comms:
   - We will schedule a 30-minute remediation call with MindBridge at 02:00 UTC (please confirm).

Risks/Notes: short-term throttles will increase latency for some in-flight requests but should prevent systemic queueing and 502s. We'll provide clear UX messaging if we trigger throttles.

— Stephanie Nguyen
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
